problems: The wall shows as plain white: no brick courses, and the light washes out its pale cream, so the brief's 'cream brick wall' does not read. Added raised brick courses over darker cream mortar, kept clear of the doorway.
The keystone shows as a thin hook or stick on top of the arch. It barely appears at the crown. Made it a bigger wedge that rests on the arch.
The transom bar sticks out past the arch tube at both ends and shows as two small black stubs. Set its ends flush with the jambs and the foot of the arch, and the jambs now stop under it.

The brick courses stop raggedly about a brick's width short of the door frame. This leaves a bare strip of mortar backing, uneven and up to ~0.1 wide, around the jambs and the arch, so the doorway looks cut out of the wall rather than built into it. Bricks should run up to the frame and be cut to fit around the jambs and arch, as in a real wall.

The bricks are far too large for the door: a 0.2 x 0.065 brick next to a 0.5-wide door is a brick about 0.36 m long. A real brick is about a quarter of a door's width, so the brick size is reduced to keep true proportions.
